MINUTES

  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING

  OCTOBER 3, 2016

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A Regular Meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by CHAIR
SCHACHTER.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

CHAIR SCHACHTER led the assembly in the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.

3.  ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Zigrang, Scott, Yoo, Chair Schachter
Commissioners Absent:  Medawar, Thomas
Staff Present:  Planning Director Wahba, Senior Planner Naughton

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG,

  TO APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE REGULAR PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING OF SEPTEMBER 6, 2016.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

None.

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  Waive reading in full of all resolutions that are presented for Planning Commission
  consideration on tonight’s agenda and all such resolutions shall be read by title only.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG,

  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEM 6-A.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  None.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 06-16; APPLICANT: Rolling Hills United Methodist
  Church; LOCATION: 26438 Crenshaw Blvd.; Demolishing the campus’ five one-story
  buildings and construction of three new buildings in the same location, resulting in an
  increase in preschool enrollment from 102 to up to 140 students. Project involves a
  Neighborhood Compatibility Determination, Variance, Grading Application, an
  amendment to Conditional Use Permit No. 101-79, and an Initial Study/Environmental
  Checklist that recommends the Lead Agency adopt a Mitigated Negative Declaration.

Planning Commission Minutes  1
October 3, 2016
 Senior Planner Naughton summarized the staff report and presented a slide show presentation
to the Commission. Afterwards she introduced Eileen Gueringer, Architect and Joseph R.
Spierer, AIA, both from Joseph Spierer Architects, Inc., and John Bellas, Engineer from Michael
Baker International, and Reverend Jonathan Chute from Rolling Hills United Methodist Church.

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG, Reverend Chute stated that there
were approximately 400 students at Country Day School.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked when the easement that crossed the horse trail that accesses
the Botanical Gardens was approved. Planning Director Wahba said that it was never approved
by the City, but that the Church and Botanical Gardens did this on their own. After complaints
from equestrians about their horses getting spooked from people crossing the trail, it went to the
Equestrian Committee and then to the City Council. The City Council put a plan in place where
the City would be given advance notice of when that easement would be accessed and signage
would be put up a few days in advance, and someone would be there in place to make sure that
there was safe crossing for pedestrians and horse traffic as well. A condition of approval has
been included in the project resolution to ensure that an agreement between the Church,
Country Day School and the Botanical Gardens remains in place to regulate the trail crossing
and to ensure that there is adequate parking for all three uses at times of large events.

COMMISSIONER YOO asked if the fence around the play area, at 4’, would be high enough.
Senior Planner Naughton stated that 4’ was the minimum height required by the State
guidelines and the plan was to keep it as unobtrusive as possible.

In response to a question from CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER, Planning Director Wahba said that
traffic impacts from construction trucks wouldn’t be a problem because this was not a huge
project and the trucks would be small, and also they would arrive and begin work at 7:00 AM
and typically leave by 3:00 PM, and would not typically take Palos Verdes Drive North.

COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG asked if anything was going to be done about the amount of traffic
making U-turns in front of Seahorse taking their kids to school. Planning Director Wahba stated
that although there is a bit of a traffic backing up at that time, that it was during a small window
of time and to his knowledge there were no accidents from it.

COMMISSIONERS SCOTT and YOO both stated that their children had some level of affiliation
with the school; however, their ability to discuss and vote on this project would not be a conflict
of interest.

COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER so ordered.

Reverend Jonathan Chute from Rolling Hills United Methodist Church spoke and gave a brief
background of the buildings, which were built in the mid-1960’s that were used by children in
Sunday School for a one to two-hour activity one day a week. Starting 1972 they offered a
preschool five days a week, so they knew eventually they needed to make an improvement. He
added that the improvements would move the facility away from Crenshaw Blvd. to open up a
larger play area for the children, and changing from five buildings to one opened up space. In
regards to the fence it was in accordance with Title 22 as far as safety, and also it was behind a
berm so it would be very unobtrusive.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER so ordered.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG,

  TO RECEIVE THE COMMENT LETTER FROM THE SANITATION DISTRICTS DATED
  SEPTEMBER 29, 2016 AND INCORPORATE THE COMMENTS BY REFERENCE
  INTO THE INITIAL STUDY/MITIGATED NEGATIVE DECLARATION, AND TO ADOPT
  RESOLUTION NO. PA-06-16, ADOPTING A MITIGATED NEGATIVE DECLARATION
  AND MITIGATION MONITORING AND REPORTING PROGRAM FOR THE PROJECT;
  AND APPROVING AN AMENDMENT TO CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT (CUP 101-79),
  GOVERNING SCHOOL USES, FOR INCREASED ENROLLMENT FROM 102 TO 140
  PRESCHOOL CHILDREN; VARIANCE FOR A FENCE IN THE REQUIRED FRONT

9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

None.

10.  DIRECTOR’S ITEMS

Planning Director Wahba stated that the next Planning Commission meeting would be
November 7th. He added that the City Council conducted a few interviews for the new Planning
Commissioner, and because of two no-shows, they were going to finish the interviews next
week.

At 7:32 p.m. CHAIR SCHACHTER adjourned the Planning Commission meeting to November
7, 2016, at 7:00 p.m.
